from.place: The open projection map used to interpret the open scalar comparison; this node isolates existing intrinsic open-adjunction definitions from the integral coefficient setting.

title: Intrinsic open coefficient adjunction data
statement: For each scheme W [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], a coefficient family consists of a sheaf of commutative rings R_W and an inverse-image identification f^{-1}R_V ≅ R_U for each scheme map f:U→V. No composition axiom is imposed on this organizing record. For an open immersion j:U→X [def-weil-open-immersion], use the exact ring-module extension j_! and restriction j^{-1}, with the ordinary adjunction localized degreewise to unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Given the two actual tensor presentations, define the inverse projection j_!(K ⊗ j^{-1}Q) → j_!K ⊗ Q as the open adjunct of unit tensor identity followed by the inverse canonical tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These are exactly the existing general definitions Coefficients, openExtension, openAdjunction, pull, openDerivedAdjunction and openProjectionInverse, independent of the later completed coefficient systems.

lean.statement:
structure Coefficients where
  ring : ∀ W : Scheme.{u}, Sheaf (ProEt.topology W) CommRingCat.{u + 1}
  pull : ∀ {U V : Scheme.{u}} (g : U ⟶ V),
    (proEtaleSheafInverseImage g CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (ring V) ≅ ring U
lean.note: Existing definitions, unchanged. Their old broad owner also covered Frobenius and integral coefficient data; this attachment isolates the general open notions to remove a spurious dependency on their own consumers.
